page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top centre, page number at the top left. Below the running head, a sermon heading, a scripture reference, and then the text opening with a woodcut initial. No marginal notes or footnotes.

main_text.p: rea non sunt ingloria in celebriaue: quemadmodum neque quia aurum preciosius est, argentum gloria precioque vacat. Quod vero pretiosius est, pretiosio[?] pretiosius est: & quod melius est, bono melius est, non malo. Qui ergo potest, virginitatis aurum retineat: si vero non possit ituc[?], matrimonij argentum recipiat. Non ergo male facit vxorem ducens, in Domino: melius autem non ducens, quod ad commoditatem praesentis vi-tae attinet. Contra hanc libertatem pugnat tyrannis Romani pontificis, sacerdotibus adimens ius contrahendi matrimonium. A-qua tyrannide cum nos liberauerit Dominus Deus, sit illi honor & gloria in aeter-num, Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO XLVII.
Lucæ 1[?].

p.i: Erat in diebus Herodis regis Iudææ, sacerdos quidam nomine Zacharias, de vice Abia, & uxor illius de filiabus Aaron, & nomen eius Elizabeth. Erant autem iusti ambo coram Deo, versantes in omnibus praeceptis & iustificationibus Domini irreprehensibiles: nec e-rat illis proles, eo quod esset Elizabeth sterilis,

page.notes: Page begins mid-sentence (fragment); the first paragraph continues from the previous page. The woodcut initial E is read as "Erat". The heading "Lucæ 1." is partly uncertain: the numeral may be "r" or "1". Printed "pretiosio pr.tiofius" appears garbled in the scan. "celebriaue" and "ituc" are doubtful readings. Italic is taken to run across the whole paragraph from "Erat" to "sterilis,", although "Domini irreprehensibiles" may be roman. No catchword or signature visible.
